summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 100-1400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 30 views. The best video, the PIR motion sensor one, got about 2,000 combined views and the most likes, shares and saves because its hook is a surprising claim about a sensor people see daily. Engagement (shares and saves) is very low overall, and the single English video did well on YouTube only, so the sample is too small to judge language.
winningPattern: Everyday sensor people meet in real life (motion sensor, street light, phone orientation) + a hook that states a surprising or counterintuitive claim ('doesn't see you!') followed by a 'Kaise?' question, in Hinglish title with 🤔 and #shorts, posted mainly to Instagram Reels. Titles that name a familiar object plus a twist outperform generic 'X kaise kaam karta hai' or niche-component titles (ultrasonic, IR, smartwatch).
doMore: Open with a bold myth-busting line ('X aapko dekhta nahi!') in the first 2 seconds
Pick sensors from daily life everyone has seen: ATM, lift, AC, fridge, traffic signal
Prioritise Instagram Reels as the main platform and cross-post to YouTube with a more searchable title
End each video with a save/share prompt like 'Dost ko bhejo jo ye sochta hai'
Test one English or bilingual title on YouTube, since the English Arduino video got 160 views there versus about 10-25 for Hindi
stopDoing: Near-duplicate topics like two smoke detector videos in 3 days
Component-focused titles with no everyday hook (IR, ultrasonic, smartwatch light)
Posting many videos in a week without varying the hook style
nextTopics: Automatic hand dryer or sanitizer dispenser

bestTimes.reason: from our own posts: these hours averaged the most views (12 posts)
